name: Ariel Tabak Outside Passing System
description: Ariel Tabak’s Outside Passing Compendium covers getting around the legs, upper-body control, leg traps and finishing routes, including gi-specific grips.
summary: Outside passing from the initial flank to the finish, with leg traps, bullfighter variations and extensive gi-grip material.
overview:
Outside Passing Compendium by Ariel Tabak focuses on the gap between getting around the legs and completing the pass. Its four volumes develop outside entries, upper-body control and finishing options, with leg-trap and cross-grip variations.

The course suits passers who can reach the flank but struggle to finish. Collar, trouser and sleeve grips give it a substantial gi-specific component.

related_content.name: Lachlan Giles Body Lock Passing System
related_content.relationship: For a dedicated no-gi course built around body-lock entries and clearing the legs from close contact.

flashcards.question: Why should a no-gi reader separate the grip-specific sections of Ariel Tabak’s Outside Passing Compendium?
flashcards.answer: The published outline names collar, pant and sleeve grips. Those sections assume gi equipment and cannot be treated as unchanged no-gi sequences.

products.title: Outside Passing Compendium
products.blurb: Four volumes on outside-passing entries and finishes, leg traps and cross-grip variations.
products.best_for: Passers whose outside entries outpace their ability to finish, especially in the gi.

guide.display_title: Ariel Tabak: Outside Passing and Finishing

fits: You get around the legs but lose the pass before securing upper-body control.
You want outside-passing options that include gi leg traps and cross-grip passing.

includes: Outside entries, high-pummel responses, side changes and progression to upper-body control.
Leg-trap finishes through leg drags, knee on belly, long steps and stacking.
Lasso and reverse De La Riva responses, north-south passing and cross-grip bullfighters.
limits: Several sections require collar, trouser or sleeve grips; the whole course does not transfer unchanged to no-gi.
